atoms.b: The Earth is made up of ((--no ++multiple)) layers. The outermost layer is called the crust. It is only between 3 and 45 miles thick, making it the ((++thinnest thickest)) layer. The tectonic plates that make up the Earth’s surface can be found here.

The layer beneath the crust is called the mantle. At around 1,800 miles thick, this is the ((++thickest thinnest)) layer. The mantle is made of hot molten rock called ((sponge ++magma)), which Earth’s tectonic plates float on top of.
The following layer is the outer core, which reaches up to ((--2 3,000)) miles deep. Here we have a mixture of liquid metals at ((distances ++temperatures)) of around 4,400°C!

At the very centre of the planet is the inner core. Even though the temperature here is as hot as the surface of the ((++Sun Moon)), the inner core is made of solid ((chocolate ++metal)). This is because the pressure is so great that everything is held together!

hint.text: The Earth’s inner core sits at about 5,400°C!

atoms.a: Do you think anybody has ever travelled to the centre of the Earth?

feedback.finish: The only reason that we know about Earth’s multiple layers is because of scientists measuring vibrations from earthquakes and doing complicated maths problems.

instruction.text: Put the Earth’s layers in order. Start with the surface at the top.
